text: The bias problem in prior knowledge motivates three auxiliary regularization terms in the Generalized Expectation Criteria framework to make GE-FL more robust.
With unbalanced labeled features on balanced and unbalanced movie datasets, incorporating the KL divergence of class distribution performs much better than GE-FL.
When balanced labeled features are used on the unbalanced movie dataset, incorporating KL divergence is much better than GE-FL because it provides the true class distribution.
LDA selects predictive labeled features without considering class balance, and GE-FL does not control this issue, so auxiliary regularization terms promote the model significantly.
The top 10 frequent words after removing stop words are used as neutral features in all experiments, implementing the proposed approach without manual annotation.
The maximum entropy regularization term controls unbalance without extra knowledge, but its uniform-category assumption creates degraded performance when violated.
Unlike the maximum entropy regularization term, KL divergence handles unbalanced corpora better by using the reference class distribution instead of assuming uniformly distributed categories.

Incorporating neutral features is simple and requires no modification of GE-FL, but it is not strong enough for extremely unbalanced labeled features, whereas the maximum entropy regularization term controls unbalance.

The proposed joint Bayesian model implements the expected benefit of word alignment information in parallel text by using crosslingual latent variables to incorporate soft role agreement between aligned constituents.

The small percentage of aligned roles probably limits the impact of cross-lingual information in the labeled-source transfer setting, consistent with only 8% of English arguments and 17% of German arguments being aligned.
The multilingual model is deficient because aligned roles are generated twice, an approximation used because an additional conditioning variable breaks Dirichlet-multinomial conjugacy.
The paper extends the superlingual latent variables idea proposed for POS tagging to SRI through crosslingual latent variables that capture role alignments in parallel corpora.
The paper uses garg2012unsupervised's Bayesian model as the monolingual basis regularized by crosslingual latent variables in its joint Bayesian model of multilingual SRI.
The Dual Decomposition (DD) based algorithm improved PP-attachment accuracy by 10% over the MSTParser baseline on 100 parallel sentences from the Hindi-English Tourism parallel corpus.
The DD algorithm's input is a parallel English-Hindi sentence pair with word alignments, while GIZA++ word-alignment errors may cascade and cause the system to underperform.
The Project Algorithm predicts target-language trees using source-language parse trees and word alignments, and its projected paths are supplied by two classifiers in a pipeline.
The DD algorithm was evaluated on 100 parallel sentences with manually annotated PP-attachment ambiguity, where it marked 64 attachments correctly in the best case.
The collected dataset addresses the lack of public datasets for interactive learning by enabling simulated interaction with users for training interactively learned policies.
Because offline evaluation of interactive dialogs is difficult when different policies produce different variants, the dataset collects all information and omits parts not requested by the policy.
The three phase dialog implements the interactive learning steps of paraphrasing, broader explanation, and correct answer collection described as the dataset's main purpose.
The dataset's 1900 dialogs and 8533 turns were collected using CrowdFlower because access to systems with real users is usually hard.
The expert annotation of user answer hints supports the answer extraction accuracy metric, which measures correct answer extraction from dialogs annotated as correctly answered.
The 702 dialogs with incorrect answer include 285 answers for general questions that annotators were forced to mark incorrect to stay consistent with Simple questions annotation.
The NLU outputs included in each file come from hand written rules using templates and keyword spotting that were used during data collection.
Character-level modeling is chosen to make the model robust to unseen KB entries because it has been previously shown to generalize well to new words not seen during training.
The semantic relevance function addresses the scale problem of millions of entities and thousands of predicates by avoiding a large output layer in the decoder.
The model's semantic relevance function is implemented as cosine similarity between decoder hidden states and KB entry embeddings to avoid an output layer with millions of nodes.
The model decodes a KB query consisting of exactly the topic entity and predicate by selecting the most likely (entity, predicate) pair from generated candidate entities and predicates.

In random-sampling experiments with 200 entities and predicates as noise samples, character-level models achieve 96.6% accuracy in predicting the correct entity while word-level models predict 45% of entities accurately.
The conclusion that character-level modeling gives a compact model that is robust to unseen entities is evidenced by identifying phrenology, whose English aliases were never seen in training.
The framework's conversational flow patterns are evaluated on 108 IQ2 debates where pre- and post-debate votes define winners, yielding Flow: 63% and Flow*: 65% accuracy.
Audience features use applause and laughter counts as rough outcome indicators because winning teams tend to receive more laughter during discussion and more applause during conclusion.
Flow features outperform length and BOW baselines despite excluding the concluding round, where winning teams tend to receive more applause.
The basic unigram-based definition of discussion points limits the robustness of idea flow analysis because it does not account for context or semantic sense.

The paper's focus on conversational flow extends previous influence studies in relatively unstructured political settings by using highly structured Oxford-style debates that control for confounding factors.
tweet2vec uses hashtag-prediction supervision to train character-based tweet embeddings and outperforms the word model on held-out hashtag prediction.

Because the word-level baseline stores only the 20K most common words and groups the rest under `UNK', tweet2vec's significantly better RW test set performance supports its advantage on out-of-vocabulary words.
The Bi-GRU encoder's character-stream input creates longer GRU input sequences than words, which increases tweet2vec's training time despite its improved performance.
The final dataset's 2039 distinct hashtags define the softmax output layer size L used to compute posterior hashtag probabilities from the tweet embedding.
tweet2vec extends the C2W model by replacing LSTM units with GRU units and generating vector representations of entire tweets from characters.
The word-level baseline's whitespace tokenization and `UNK' grouping instantiate the preprocessing and unseen-word limitations attributed to word-based methods.

The noisy Twitter phenomena of slang, misspellings, emojis and special characters motivate the character based approach, whose predictions show robustness to spelling mistakes and effective interpretation of emojis and other special characters.
The assumption that posts with the same hashtags should have close embeddings is operationalized by optimizing categorical cross-entropy loss between predicted and true hashtags.
tweet2vec's character lookup table models 2829 unique characters, whereas the word-level baseline stores word vectors for the 20K most common words.
The simple voting scheme that combines CNNs and RNNs is the ensemble voting process used to report ensemble results.
The ranking layer whose integration has a large impact on RNN performance corresponds to the ranking loss function applied to train the models.
The extended middle context addresses the max-pooling risk of choosing values far from the relation mention by splitting context into two parts and repeating the middle context.
Connectionist bi-directional RNN models combine all intermediate hidden layers for their final decision by adding a connection to the previous combined hidden layer.
The additional hidden layer connections that have a large impact on RNN performance are the feature defining connectionist bi-directional RNNs.
The CNN and RNN models combined by voting were evaluated with the official scoring script using macro F1 score on 2,717 test sentences.

Because translating into a target language with a missing distinction requires background knowledge to resolve ambiguity, German `sie' or `ihr' Winograd schemas should challenge automatic machine translation.
The GENIA data set has 27% unseen words (dictionary misses) in the pretrained word2vec model, supporting why EMB cannot adapt to the medical domain without retraining.
Because middle-quartile dogmatism annotations had agreement no better than chance, the classifier used only top and bottom quartiles, yielding 2,500 balanced Reddit training comments.
Linguistic features boosted BOW AUC from 0.853 to 0.881 within Reddit and from 0.776 to 0.791 on held out New York Times comments.
The held out New York Times testing data had 500 total comments and was not referred to during feature construction, supporting domain-independence testing.
The claim that linguistic features generalize across new domains is evidenced by their boost to 0.791 on held out New York Times comments.
The Introduction's claim that dogmatic posts tend not to verbalize cognition is supported by LIWC insight terms being associated with non-dogmatic comments at 0.83 odds.
The Introduction's claim that less confident language tends to be less dogmatic is supported by tentativeness being associated with absence of dogmatism at 0.88 odds.
The model trained on only 5,000 annotated posts was used to analyze millions of other Reddit posts, where a diverse set of topics are colored by dogmatic language.

The linear regression model using the dogmatism levels of A1 and B to predict A2 found B's coefficient positively associated with dogmatism, supporting engagement with a dogmatic comment making a user more dogmatic.
The A1 → B → A2 conversation structure controls for A's initial dogmatism, so the positive B coefficient indicates B's dogmatism affects A2 beyond A1's dogmatism level.
The paper's computational model applied to Reddit extends Ertel's small lexicon approach by using supervised models based on a broader set of linguistic categories.
The first corpus of social media posts annotated with dogmatism scores enabled the predictive model applied to Reddit that discovered behavioral predictors of dogmatism.
The conclusion's behavioral predictors of dogmatism correspond to the activity, breadth, focus, and engagement metrics computed from 1000 users and 10 million posts.
QRNNs address standard RNNs' inability to parallelize very long sequences by allowing parallel computation across timestep and minibatch dimensions while preserving sequence order.
QRNNs combine CNNs' increased parallelism and better scaling to long sequences with RNN-like dependence on overall sequence order.
Because QRNNs lack recurrent weights, variational inference–based dropout does not apply, so zoneout was extended to the QRNN architecture.
The zoneout extension described for QRNNs was applied on the Penn Treebank as dropout with ratio 0.1 on the forget gates of the QRNN.
On the Penn Treebank, applying a small amount of zoneout removed the need for early stopping and achieved competitive perplexity to the variational LSTM of BIBREF13.
The sequence-to-sequence QRNN architecture evaluated on IWSLT German–English spoken-domain translation uses a QRNN encoder and a modified QRNN, enhanced with attention, as decoder.

The modified decoder that supplements convolution outputs with the final encoder hidden state avoids the representational-power limitation of feeding only the last encoder hidden state into recurrent pooling.
On IWSLT German–English spoken-domain translation, the QRNN outperformed the character-level LSTM and almost matched a word-level attentional baseline.
Because all labels in each dataset are mapped to anger, joy, sadness, surprise, the Affective Text, Fairy Tales, and ISEAR benchmarks evaluate the same final emotion labels.
The costly and difficult creation of manually annotated datasets motivates the paper's Facebook-reaction distant supervision for training Support Vector Machine models.
The final models are evaluated on the Affective Text test set, Fairy Tales dataset, and ISEAR dataset after development on 250 annotated sentences.

The gating mechanism proposed to balance structure and text representations is empirically supported by gate activations showing text information plays a more important role for low-frequency entities.

The attention mechanism introduced to select relation-relevant text information achieves the best performance on FB15K, where “Jointly(A-LSTM)” is significantly higher than baseline methods on mean rank.
The joint models that combine structure and text representations with a gating mechanism surpass TransE on all metrics in link prediction experiments on WN18 and FB15k.
The paper addresses the challenge of entities with few or no facts by using text descriptions, and experiments report that textual information largely alleviates the issue of sparsity.
The attentive LSTM encoder extends the LSTM encoder by using relation-dependent attention to construct contextual text encodings, addressing the LSTM encoder's context-independent representation.
The max-margin training criterion requires golden triplets to score higher than corrupted triplets, and the objective minimizes a margin loss with standard L2 regularization weighted by η.
The proposed models are evaluated on WN18 and FB15K, subsets of WordNet and Freebase chosen because their text descriptions are easily publicly available.
The threshold-based triplet classification setting on WN18 and FB15K shows that joint encoding models are effective and outperform the baseline method.
On FB15K, “Jointly(A-LSTM)” reaches 91.5% classification accuracy, supporting the conclusion that jointly representation learning with gating mechanism is effective.
Morphological segmentation with morfessor 2.0 and Tamil annotation data improved BLEU precision values in the RNNMorph model for agglutinative Tamil.
The word2vec embeddings trained on 569,772 Tamil sentences slightly increased BLEU scores when used to refine the baseline RNNSearch system.
The phrase-based SMT system used the same corpus and 569,772 monolingual Tamil sentences for its language model, yet performed inferior to RNNSearch.
The structural discordance between English and Tamil sentences motivated global attention in the Bahdanau et al. Bahdanau2014 attention-based translation model.
The scarce Tamil parallel corpus and neural translation models' heavy corpus requirement jointly make English–Tamil neural MT especially difficult.
The trade-off between domain specificity and corpus size was addressed by selecting 197,792 sentences from different corpora across various domains.
The BLEU score's micro-average precision computation limits interpretation of RNNMorph's large BLEU increase because morphological segmentation increases word units per sentence.

Human evaluation on about 100 test-set sentences with 50 native annotators found RNNMorph better than RNNSearch + Word2Vec, supporting the BLEU-score increase as actual translation-performance improvement.
Morphological segmentation decreased the target vocabulary size but increased average sentence lengths, creating model complexity and more input units (morphs) per sentence for RNNMorph.
The stacked generalization ensemble of Text, Occu, Intro, and Inter L0 classifiers improves the test-set INLINEFORM0 from 0.534 to 0.643 and INLINEFORM1 from 0.477 to 0.564.
The paper's goal of examining the link between language and occupational class is supported by experiments showing that word choice in users' posts correlates with their industry.
Stacking improves the content-based classifier's overall accuracy from up to 0.534 to 0.643 on the test dataset.
The content-based classifier's overall accuracy of up to 0.534 is a large improvement over the majority class baseline of 0.188, while stacking reaches 0.643.
Because AntSynNET uses patterns as main indicators of word pair co-occurrence, patterns representing both antonymous and synonymous pairs limit precision.
The combined AntSynNET model concatenates word vectors with LSTM-encoded pattern vectors and is evaluated on a dataset split into 70% train, 25% test, and 5% validation sets.
AntSynNET's distance label is initialized with 10 dimensions and measures path distance between target word nodes in the syntactic tree.
The challenge that antonyms and synonyms often occur in similar contexts is addressed by AntSynNET's use of lexico-syntactic patterns to distinguish antonyms from synonyms.
The pattern-based model feeds frequency-weighted LSTM pattern vectors into logistic regression and predicts a word pair as positive, i.e., antonymous, when probability is larger than 0.5.
The combined AntSynNET model uses both co-occurrence distribution of the words and syntactic path patterns, extending the pattern-based model that uses patterns alone.
Using the English Wikipedia dump from June 2016 parsed with spaCy, the models induce patterns only for word pairs with at least five patterns after filtering patterns occurring less than five times.

The two proposed models whose performance the distance feature enhances more effectively than the direction feature are the two AntSynNET approaches whose resulting vectors were fed into logistic regression.
Although the methods rely on dLCE word embeddings that represent information collected from lexical resources, the conclusion says the two proposed models only rely on corpus data.
The paper addresses the difficulty of sarcasm detection with traditional NLP tools and techniques by augmenting textual features with cognitive features extracted with eye-tracking.

The conjecture that reading sarcastic texts induces distinctive eye movement patterns is supported by the observed average fixation duration per word being at least 1.5 times more for sarcastic texts.
The hypothesis that distinctive eye-movement patterns form the crux of sarcasm detection is validated using a database of 1,000 short texts, each having 10-40 words.

Because incorrect annotations are not discarded, the assumption that most readers identify sarcasm limits distortion of averaged eye-movement parameters for both regular and multi-instance based classifiers.
Gaze, defined as simple and complex cognitive features with readability and word count features, is evaluated through stratified 10-fold cross validation on 994 examples.
The MILR classifier using the complete set of features improves over joshi2015harnessing textual sarcasm features alone, with a significant difference of p(two-tailed) = 0.02 and odds-ratio of 1.43.
The extended feature-set that improved the success rate of the sarcasm detector by 3.7%, over the best available system combines gaze and linguistic features, which predict correctly in sentence 4.

The system's use of cognitive features obtained from readers' eye-movement data is supported by example sentence 1, where gaze features possibly helped predict the label successfully despite textual features failing.
The general approach of augmenting traditional linguistic features with cognitive features may be useful in other NLP sub-areas where considering textual clues alone does not prove to be sufficient.

The example cases from the experiment with stratified 80%-20% train-test split include sentence 4, where gaze features alone false-indicate presence of incongruity but the combined system predicts correctly.

The example cases from the experiment with stratified 80%-20% train-test split include sentence 3, a false-negative case where gaze features and the complete set of features account for erroneous prediction.

The conclusion that simple lexical features and reduced feature sets can produce comparable results to the much larger feature dataset is supported by optimal F1-score performances at low percentiles for fatigue or loss of energy, disturbed sleep, depressive symptoms, and no evidence of depression.

The paper's stated need to better understand the predictive power of supervised machine learning classifiers and feature groups is addressed by two feature study experiments: a feature ablation study and a feature elimination study.
Because SimpleQuestions has 14% unseen golden test relations, breaking relation names into word sequences addresses the zero-shot relation detection problem.
Hierarchical matching combines word-level and relation-level representations because word-level has better generalization while relation-level captures global information.
Deep BiLSTM question representations are designed to match relation words and relation names, which correspond to short phrases and longer phrases.
Residual learning addresses the training difficulty of naive hierarchical matching by making two-layer question representations comparable and complementary.
The additional entity re-ranking step addresses entity linking ambiguity by using relation scores to distinguish candidates such as TV writer and baseball player “Mike Kelley”.
The KBQA pipeline uses HR-BiLSTM relation scores first to re-rank entity candidates and then to score relations for each re-ranked candidate entity.
The improved relation detector enables the simple KBQA system to achieve state-of-the-art results by supporting entity re-ranking and more accurate relation detection.
Attention-based hierarchical matching performs below HR-BiLSTM, while HR-BiLSTM uses residual connections to make two-layer representations comparable.
HR-BiLSTM performs hierarchical matching between questions and KB relations, and its residual and deep structures contribute to its good performance.
The gold semantic parses in SimpleQuestions and WebQSP enable direct relation detection evaluation, where HR-BiLSTM's hierarchical matching improves both datasets.
The system outputs an < entity, relation (or core-chain) > pair using s_rerank and s_rel, and removing the entity re-ranking step significantly decreases KBQA scores.
Since the re-ranking step relies on relation detection models, HR-BiLSTM contributes to KBQA performance both as the improved relation detector and through entity re-ranking.

The paper's proposed architecture addresses the lack of methods and tools to design and engineer coordination and mediation among chatbots and humans by supporting coordinated aware chatbots in a multiparty conversation.
Because most existing chatbots from ELIZA BIBREF11 until modern state-of-the-art ones are Dyadic Chatbots, they do not properly handle a group chat with many users and many chatbots.
Cicero claimed that people should know when to talk in a conversation, and turn-taking is how a participant determines when it is appropriate to make an utterance and how that is accomplished.
The hybrid rule and machine learning-based MPCS addresses the lack of platforms for coordinated multiparty chatbots with governance or mediation by using a Hub and mediator chatbots.
The Parsing phase supports context reasoning by storing metadata in the Context, while most context reasoning approaches use rules, logics and knowledge bases.
The Intent Flow uses Entities and Features to choose the next answer node, and the Frame-based approach fills frame slots represented by Entities and Features from dependency trees.
The Hub broadcasts messages to every Member and may enforce norms, supporting the Filtering phase's decision about who should reply to the utterance.
The 1NN classifier's easy addition of new intent classes and samples enabled the training set to grow from 37 to 63 classes and from 415 to 659 samples.
SVM was chosen after the training set became stable enough, and it reached accuracies about 12 percentage points higher than 1NN under leave-one-out validation.
CognIA's Compute action implements investment simulation by having the savings account chatbot compute EQREF90 and the certificate of deposit compute EQREF92.
The validation framework's collection of response times enabled Test 1 to show that all chatbots (Mediator, CDBExpert, and SavingsAccountExpert) responded all expected responses before 30 seconds.
The tests' goal of verifying reasonable time and computing resources is supported by Test 1's finding that response 19 reached 20 seconds.
Test 2 used eight concurrent simulated users and 240 seconds, eight times Test 1's 30 seconds, to compare response times with one user.
The validation framework developed as a new component of SABIA's system architecture was used to validate CognIA's implementation through integration tests.
The framework's two-part division supports its stated goals: one part gathers resource consumption metrics inside SABIA, while the other checks correct responses and response times.
The RALSTM Decoder refines the original input token w_t using the attentive DA representation d_t and hidden context h_t-1 before the traditional LSTM controls information flow.
The proposed generators trained with negative log-likelihood and l_2 regularization are assessed by experiments using several metrics, datasets, and model architectures to compare to prior methods.
The proposed model learns from unaligned data by jointly training sentence planning and surface realization, while experiments assess its effectiveness against prior methods.
The RNN Decoder input includes an attentive DA representation d_t, and the Aligner computes d_t using attention weights over slot-value pairs.
The proposed models' better performance across all domains in all test cases is measured using the BLEU and the slot error rate ERR.
The proposed models were compared against three strong baselines: HLSTM, SCLSTM, and Enc-Dec.
The general models trained by merging all four domains and tested in each individual domain showed RALSTM better than Enc-Dec and SCLSTM in BLEU and ERR.
The adaptation models trained on merged Restaurant and Hotel data and fine tuned on laptop domain showed RALSTM outperforming previous models with sufficient and limited in-domain data.
The conclusion of consistent improvement in BLEU and ERR is supported by extensive experiments showing better performance across all domains in all test cases.
The harder Laptop and TV NLG tasks require learning partial realization of concepts and recombining them for unseen DAs, which the LSTM encoder and Aligner help address.
The first study to target stance detection in Turkish tweets provides a publicly available stance-annotated data set of 700 tweets.
The baseline SVM classifiers trained with unigrams on the 700-tweet data set were evaluated with 10-fold cross-validation using precision, recall, and F-Measure.
The 700-tweet data set is balanced with 175 Favor and 175 Against tweets for each of Galatasaray (Target-1) and Fenerbahçe (Target-2).
The paper's stated SVM classifiers using unigram, bigram, and hashtag features correspond to separate experiments with unigrams, bigrams, and unigrams plus hashtags.
The 10-fold cross-validation results presented as reference results by prospective systems are the evaluation results of the SVM classifiers on the 700-tweet data set.
The encoder-decoder-reconstructor addresses over-translation and under-translation by using back-translation to enforce agreement between source and target sentences.

The encoder-decoder-reconstructor evaluated on English-Japanese and Japanese-English translation tasks significantly improves BLEU scores by 1.01 points on ASPEC and 1.37 points on NTCIR in English-Japanese translation.
The encoder-decoder-reconstructor without pre-training worsens translation accuracy, supporting the conclusion that pre-training the forward translation model is required.
The encoder-decoder-reconstructor reduces redundant word occurrences and alleviates repeating and missing words in English-Japanese translation while maintaining translation quality.

The encoder-decoder-reconstructor uses the standard encoder-decoder as attention-based NMT proposed by DzmitryBahdana2014, which predicts output words using weights of each hidden state of the encoder.
Unlike coverage vector or PBSMT-based methods, the encoder-decoder-reconstructor uses back-translation and needs no additional parameters such as coverage vector or a PBSMT system for testing.

The encoder-decoder-reconstructor directly penalizes translation mismatch by considering back-translation, whereas Meng2016 and Feng2016 attention mechanisms indirectly reduce repeating and missing words.

The encoder-decoder-reconstructor framework that improved BLEU scores and alleviated repeating and missing words on Chinese-English translation is evaluated here on English-Japanese and Japanese-English translation tasks.

Because available annotated data is very limited and additional training data has the biggest impact on improving performance, the paper's artificial error generation methods address a key bottleneck for error detection.
The SMT framework that trains a model to translate from correct into incorrect sentences is implemented by treating error-corrected sentences as source and original learner sentences as target.
The pattern-based method extends Felice2014a by relaxing the restriction to only five error types, and its all-error-type coverage is credited with consistently improving performance.

The artificial data evaluated on FCE test data and two alternative annotations of the CoNLL 2014 Shared Task dataset was generated from 450K corrected FCE tokens and 270K English Vocabulary Profile tokens.
The multilingual g2p system treats words in standard orthography as source sequences and IPA representations as targets using a neural encoder–decoder model with attention.

Because multilingual g2p has similar but different and possibly contradictory spelling rules, the authors choose a data-driven sequence-to-sequence model implemented as a neural encoder–decoder with attention.
LangID and NoLangID have identical structure otherwise, so the considerable result improvement from using a language ID token isolates that token as the differing factor.
On the 229 languages used for adapted wFST results, the best LangID performance came from LangID-All trained on all 311 languages in the Wiktionary training corpus.
The wFST baseline compared with LangID and NoLangID is the deri2016grapheme system whose adapted results cover 229 languages.

The uninterpretable structure of language ID token vectors makes estimating embeddings for unseen languages difficult, motivating externally constructed typological representations available in Phoible and WALS.
Emoji embeddings BIBREF16, learned from emoji descriptions, give better results than using plain GloVe and Edinburgh embeddings in word-vector combination experiments.

sefe's shared context vectors and group-specific embedding vectors are evaluated on ArXiv papers, U.S. Senate speeches, and supermarket grocery shopping data, where sefe outperforms efe in held-out log-likelihood.
The lack of data in the naïve per-group embedding approach motivates sefe's hierarchical modeling and amortization, which share statistical strength among embedding vectors.

Sharing context vectors in sefe reduces parameters and unites group-specific embeddings in the same space, avoiding the ad-hoc postprocessing needed when learning a separate embedding model for each group.
For supermarket purchases broken down by month, sefe uses the Poisson conditional distribution because it is more appropriate for count data.
For text corpora, sefe uses conditional Bernoulli distributions with a fixed-size window context, while the empirical study applies the Bernoulli distribution to text data.
Amortization controls the number of parameters by making group-specific embedding vectors the output of neural networks that take global embedding vectors as input.

Because AER only takes the most attended word into account while attention loss considers the entire attention distribution, their agreement for the two systems provides complementary evidence about attention-alignment differences.

The paper's crowdsourced pure emotion lexicon addresses beyond polarity studies' expert-based, single-emotion-per-term limitations by using Plutchik's eight basic emotions and crowd-identified linguistic elements.
The CrowdFlower task's three main classes correspond to the task interface choices Emotion evoking, Intensifying context and None, with eight basic emotions and Amplifying or Weakening options.

Because existing spamming elimination methods require gold standards or objective tasks, the subjective no-gold-standard crowdsourcing task uses a filter relying only on obtained annotations and assessment.
The 40% single annotation filtering check excluded annotations from the more than seventy thousands received, leaving only 22 thousand annotations for 9737 term groups in the final PEL.

Because two experts cost as much as nineteen Crowdflower contributors and the crowd is a stricter evaluator with significantly lower costs and higher scalability, evaluation can be performed by the crowd instead of experts.
The low single annotation reliability agreement caused by few annotators and many possible categories is addressed by additional annotations, which increase k and certainty of classification.

The number of crowd evaluations provides strictness freedom because varying agreement levels use two, three, or four valid evaluations, while high agreement makes crowd and expert evaluations almost identical.
The PA system's computer-readable interaction data enables automated text-mining analysis of supervisor assessment and peer feedback text from 4528 employees in a large multi-national IT company.
The paper's sentence classification focuses on STRENGTH, WEAKNESS and SUGGESTION, and SVM with ADWS kernel BIBREF18 produced the best results for this non-topical classification.
After sentence classification identified STRENGTH sentences, clustering was applied to 12742 predicted STRENGTH sentences to discover broad categories among strengths.
Mapping sentences in the 3 classes to the 15 attributes defined by HR managers is a multi-class multi-label classification problem evaluated on dataset D2.
Logistic Regression classifier produced the best results for the topical classification that maps supervisor assessment sentences to predefined broad perspectives on performance.
The ILP-based summarization technique selects candidate phrases from peer feedback comments and was evaluated against manual summaries using ROUGE BIBREF22 unigram score over 100 employees.
s2sL addresses the low data resource problem caused by deep architectures requiring large annotated data by simultaneously considering two samples to train the classifier.
Because s2s data representation has output labels with more than one active unit, s2s-MLP uses sigmoid activation and binary cross-entropy instead of softmax.
s2s-MLP is trained using the s2s data representation format and adam optimizer, with an input layer accepting two samples simultaneously.
In s2sL testing, each test sample is combined with preselected reference samples from any of the two classes, and voting over s2s-MLP outputs gives the predicted label.
The conclusion that s2sL handles low resourced data imbalance is supported by Anger/Happy classification, where s2sL outperforms MLP, Eusboost, and MWMOTE at lower training data amounts.
Under 5-fold cross validation with different proportions of training data, s2sL outperforms MLP especially at low resource conditions on Speech/Music and Neutral/Sad classification.
The proposed s2sL is validated on Speech/Music discrimination using GTZAN Music-Speech dataset and on emotion classification using Berlin speech emotion database (EMO-DB).
The s2s framework generates multiple instances of the same test sample by combining it with preselected reference samples, enabling voting-based decision making.

The study's meta-data analysis of 1 785 855 tweets found significant differences in followers, URLs, and user verification, supporting its preliminary characterization of political fake news on Twitter.
The study defined viral tweets as retweeted more than 1000 times, and the collected sample contained 1327 such tweets produced by 643 users.
After duplicates were eliminated and an expert manually inspected tweet text, 136 of the 1327 viral tweets were identified as potentially containing fake news.
The statistically significant larger number of URLs in viral tweets containing fake news supports the discussion's hypothesis that number of URLs could help single-out fake news in Twitter.

Manual inspection showing 117 viral fake-news tweets supported Donald Trump and 8 supported Hillary Clinton provides evidence for the discussion's claim that viral fake news content was highly polarized.

Because task specific word embeddings capture SMP specific and topic specific style, transferring only learned word embeddings in TL2 dramatically improved recall and significantly improved precision over TL1.
TL3 transfers learned word embeddings and network weights but does not significantly improve over TL2, indicating learned word embeddings are the key knowledge gained by DNN models.
The Twitter dataset's sexism and racism focus is reflected in learned embeddings where slave is similar to targets of racism and sexism, unlike the personal attack Wikipedia dataset.
The paper's three datasets instantiate the three social network types named in the Introduction: Formspring, Twitter, and Wikipedia talk pages.
The four DNN models CNN, LSTM, BLSTM, and BLSTM with attention were evaluated with five-fold cross-validation after Keras implementation and standard preprocessing.
Using a window size of one lets BV2009 stop with fewer annotations than a window size of three without losing much F-Measure, supporting smaller window sizes as mitigation.
Larger batch percents generate fewer models, giving BV2009 fewer stopping points and causing somewhat sub-optimal stopping with very large batch percents.
The tension between smaller batch sizes for learning efficiency and larger batch sizes for development speed motivates analyzing stopping method parameters such as window size.
Because KBC assumes known entities and relations while conversations may contain unknown ones, OKBC removes that assumption and generalizes KBC for knowledge learning in conversations.
LiLi addresses C-PR's inability to handle unknown query components by interactive knowledge acquisition that reduces OKBC to KBC and makes inference feasible.
LiLi's RL model formulates query-specific inference strategies for OKBC, while its lifelong prediction model predicts whether a triple should be in the KB.
LiLi retains newly acquired facts in the KB through the Knowledge Store, whose KB is initialized with base KB triples and updated over time.
LiLi's prediction model uses lifelong learning to transfer weights from a past most similar task, addressing underfitting from models trained on a few examples.
In the running example, LiLi detects unknown “Obama” and “CitizenOf”, acquires a clue for “CitizenOf”, then asks a connecting link for “Obama” before enumerating paths.
LiLi is evaluated on Freebase FB15k and WordNet INLINEFORM0 using Avg. MCC and avg. +ve F1 score for predictive performance.
Because none of the existing KBC methods can solve the OKBC problem, the experiments use various versions of LiLi as baselines.
Sep disables LL by not transferring past learned weights, and LiLi outperforms Sep, supporting the effectiveness of the lifelong learning mechanism.
F-th) uses fixed prediction threshold 0.5 instead of relation-specific threshold INLINEFORM0, and LiLi's improvement over F-th) on Freebase supports relation-specific threshold INLINEFORM0.
BG fills missing or connecting links blindly with “@-RelatedTo-@" and no guessing mechanism, while LiLi's guessing mechanism works better than BG.
w/o PTS does not ask for additional clues via past task selection, and LiLi's past task selection mechanism improves performance over w/o PTS.
LiLi is proposed for solving the OKBC problem, and experimental results showed effectiveness in predictive quality and strategy formulation ability.

The third pilot's scenario-centered question collection was adopted for the final dataset because text-centered pilots produced lexically close questions or questions that did not make sense with other texts.
Because questions and texts were collected independently, answer collection required categorizing each text–question pair before plausible correct and incorrect answer candidates were formulated.
The script-based category used during answer collection corresponds to the final dataset's 3,827 questions that require commonsense knowledge, i.e. 27.4%.
MCScript's baseline evaluation uses accuracy to compare text-based questions with questions that require common sense, categories defined during answer collection.
The neural models evaluated on MCScript use 100-dimensional GloVe vectors to initialize token representations and refine the embeddings during training.
Two trained annotators agreed with the gold standard in 98.2 % of cases, supporting the claim that Human performance shows that the dataset is highly reliable.

Because each correct answer has a low overlap with the text by design and the overlap model selects high-overlap answers, the pure word overlap baseline performs worst, with an accuracy of INLINEFORM0.
MCScript questions were collected based on script scenarios, rather than individual texts, whereas previous datasets do not explicitly address commonsense knowledge.
EqEmb treats equations as singleton words and models them with surrounding words, addressing the problem that most equations occur only once.
EqEmb was evaluated on arXiv articles from NLP, IR, AI and ML and outperformed previous embedding models across all collections.
EqEmb-U extends EqEmb by treating equations as sentences of variables, symbols and operators, and further improves performance.
Comparisons using pseudo log-likelihood against b-emb, CBOW, GloVe and PV-DM showed EqEmb outperform previous embedding models.
EqEmb's two-pass training fixes word interaction and feature vectors before modeling equations, testing whether singleton word meanings can be learned from fixed word vectors.
EqEmb uses a word-equation context window that includes equations in a larger window, and the equation context can have a larger window than the word context.
EqEmb-U tokenizes equations into SLT tuples and defines equation-level representations by averaging the representations of their constituent units.
NLI-PT addresses the need to combine Portuguese learner corpora for sufficient NLI data by collecting data from COPLE2, Leiria corpus, and PEAPL2.
NLI-PT addresses the challenge of different data formats by converting data from COPLE2, PEAPL2, and Leiria corpus to a unified data format.
NLI-PT addresses the POS-only annotation limitation of PEAPL2 and COPLE2 by uniformly annotating data at POS and syntax levels.
The first Portuguese NLI baseline used a simple linear SVM classifier with a bag of words model on five L1s and achieved 70% accuracy.
The 70% accuracy baseline is limited because NLI-PT is not balanced by topic and the experiment does not account for topic bias.
NLI-PT fills the published-research gap on Portuguese NLI by providing the first Portuguese dataset compiled for NLI.
NLI-PT uses the 15 L1s from COPLE2 as its reference set, and its final 1,868 texts were written by speakers of 15 L1s.
The baseline experiment used Chinese, English, German, Italian, and Spanish, which are among the 15 L1s included in NLI-PT.
NLI-PT supports future syntactic-feature experiments because it was uniformly annotated at POS and syntax levels.
The 50 models with different random seeds were evaluated on 4 test sets of 2000 samples, and all models performed above 99% on Standard while nonstandard deviations reached 20.63.
The Standard test set has lengths 5-10 and no repeats, matching training inputs, and all models perform above 99% on it.
The Short and Long test sets use strings of length 1-4 and 11-15, and some seeds give performances above 95% for either set.
The NUS is trained on DSTC2 dialogues and used to train a reinforcement learning based SDS policy, outperforming the ABUS on cross-model evaluation and real users.

The limited state space and likely absence of the optimal dialogue strategy in recorded corpora motivate transforming the static corpus into a user simulator that can explore strategies not in the recorded corpus.
The NUS outputs natural language, addressing the semantic-level limitation that training a DM policy with joint SLU and belief tracking is not possible without a natural-language user simulator.
The NUS generates its own goal and possibly changes it during a dialogue, while the Goal Generator updates the goal when the SDS outputs the canthelp dialogue act.
The method transforming DSTC2 goal-labels into deployable labels is needed because DSTC2 turn-specific labels predict the future and would not be available when training a policy with the NUS.
The NUS uses a single layer LSTM for both the RNN encoder and decoder, and the decoder terminates decoding when it generates the end-of-sentence (<EOS>) token.

Because deterministic beam-search prevents the NUS from covering the full breadth of user behaviour, beam-search with sampling makes the NUS non-deterministic and diverse, with 2 beams giving a good trade-off.
The Goal Generator samples DSTC2 constraints with probabilities estimated from the DSTC2 data set, while the ontology defines the possible goals and slot values.
Because the only fair comparison is indirect evaluation of policies trained with each US, the cross-model evaluation showing NUS-trained policies perform well on both USs supports NUS over ABUS.
The human evaluation setup selected policies from the five cross-model policies, and its results show NUS-trained policies outperformed ABUS-trained policies with real users.
The conclusion that the NUS excelled on both evaluation tasks is supported by cross-model SR results and human evaluation reward and success rate results.
The overfitting concern used to motivate choosing policies best on the NUS and ABUS is supported by the observation that the best policy on the NUS was not best on the ABUS.
The human evaluation used 1000 dialogues with 250 per policy, and the best NUS-trained policy achieved 93.4% success rate and 13.8 average rewards.
The cross-model evaluation after 4000 training dialogues used success rate (SR), defined as satisfying both the user's constraints and requests, to compare NUS and ABUS policies.
The proposed approach addresses language-dependent resource requirements by translating test sets to English and reusing an English RNN model without test-language resources.
The statistically significant outperformance claim is supported by Tukey HSD test results showing RNN accuracies significantly different from majority and lexicon-based baselines.
The multilingual evaluation used Spanish, Turkish, Dutch, and Russian restaurant reviews from SemEval-2016 Challenge Task 5, where RNN outperformed both baselines in all four datasets.
The general-to-specific RNN training strategy used Amazon reviews for initial training and Yelp restaurant reviews and Kaggle restaurant reviews for domain specialization.
The reliance on machine translation creates a limitation because non-English words would not have word embeddings, which would dramatically affect system effectiveness.
The lexicon-based baseline used SentiWordNet token scores, and its below-majority result for Spanish restaurant reviews supports the claim that translating data and using lexicons is insufficient.
The 3543 English-Hindi code-mixed tweets collected after removing 4161 English and 2774 Hindi tweets were evaluated with 10-fold cross validation.
The corpus whose tweets were manually classified into humorous and non-humorous classes achieved Fleiss' Kappa agreement of 0.821.
The language tags assigned to each token were used to separate words by language when preparing feature vectors for the classification model.
Hashtag decomposition in preprocessing enabled common words in hashtags to be included in the feature vector.
N-grams, described as language independent and efficient for classifying text, proved to be the most efficient in all classification models.
The corpus collected from domains like `sports', `politics', `entertainment' can be further extended to include tweets from other domains.

The PRU addresses the parameter and generalizability limitation of increasing input and context vector dimensions by using pyramidal transformation and grouped linear transformation to learn high-dimensional representations with fewer parameters.

Because the input vector is a shared dense word embedding and the context vector is highly contextualized, the PRU separately applies pyramidal transformation to input vectors and grouped linear transformation to context vectors.

Ablations show that using grouped linear transformation for context vectors reduces recurrent unit parameters by about 75% but drops performance by about 11%, clarifying the PRU's parameter-performance trade-off.
The experiments set the number of pyramidal levels to two and use average pooling for sub-sampling, while ablation results show average pooling performs best among the PRU sampling methods.
The paper fills the gap in studies of neural models with large-scale datasets over 100K by evaluating CNN, RNN, and their variants on Hate and Abusive Speech on Twitter.
The context-tweet feature designed to avoid data dependency yields CNN with context tweets scoring the highest recall and F1 for “hateful" labels.
The context-tweet feature designed to avoid data dependency yields RNN models with context tweets having the highest recall for “abusive" tweets.
Although HybridCNN outperformed word-level and character-level CNNs in prior abusive language detection, HybridCNN does not improve the baseline CNN model in this study.
The LTC method applied to bidirectional GRU networks provides the most accurate results in detecting abusive language, while RNN with LTC modules have the highest accuracy score.

Character-level features significantly decrease classification accuracy for CNN and RNN models, which the paper attributes to lack of labeled data and significant imbalance among the different labels.

Character-level representations improve F1 scores of SVM and RF classifiers because traditional machine learning classifiers were trained only with the most significant character elements using TF-IDF values.
The RNN-LTC model, a variant suffering from data insufficiency, achieves the highest F1 score for “spam" (0.551), while CNN with context tweets achieves the highest for “hateful" (0.309).
The paper's proposed recursive neural network model addresses social-media parsing difficulties by minimizing syntactic parsing and capturing relations between discourse arguments.
The 3,268 Facebook status update messages with 1,598 causality messages were split into 80% training, 10% tuning, and 10% evaluation for all models.
The LSTM classifier's superiority for causal explanation identification is supported by the Linear SVM obtaining lowest F1 while the LSTM model made the best identification performance.
The claim that feature-based models work best for causality prediction is supported by SVM and random forest classifier performing better than LSTM.
The relatively small dataset for the high complexity of the model led the authors to add a dropout layer (p=0.3) between the Word-level LSTM and the DA-level LSTM.
For causal explanation identification, removing the DA-level LSTM layer caused 0.061 F1 drop, supporting the benefit of considering relations across discourse arguments of the whole message.
The paper's causal explanation analysis subtasks of causality prediction and causal explanation identification correspond to the reported weighted F1 performance analysis over both tasks.
The complete pipeline of CP and CEI, which starts from all of test data, achieved an $F1=0.868$ at identifying discourse arguments that are causal explanations.

The inevitable limitation on the size of our dataset might have limited performances of more complex models, while the combination of the linear model and the RNN-based model of our pipeline obtained both the high performance and efficiency.
The complete pipeline of CP and CEI evaluates the final accuracy of CEI predictions under an applied setting where one does not already know whether a document has a causal explanation, unlike CEI.
For NLI, SNLI and MultiNLI use fixed GloVe pretrained word embeddings, 300D encoder states, and a 1024D MLP, and the best model achieves 87.0% accuracy on SNLI.

For SST, models use 300D GloVe vectors, 2-layer 150D or 300D encoders, and a 300D MLP classifier with tuned word embeddings, achieving new state-of-the-art accuracy on SST-2 and competitive accuracy on SST-5.
KAR addresses the data hunger and noise robustness gap by using WordNet-extracted inter-word semantic connections to explicitly assist its attention mechanisms.
The WordNet-based data enrichment method supplies the positional inter-word semantic connections that KAR uses to construct enhanced context embeddings for knowledge aided mutual attention.
The hyper-parameter INLINEFORM6 limits semantic relation chains, thereby controlling how many inter-word semantic connections can be extracted as general knowledge.
KAR's knowledge aided self attention uses pre-extracted general knowledge to restrict coarse-memory fusion to a precise subset of semantically connected passage words.
KAR's coarse memory layer uses knowledge aided mutual attention to produce question-aware passage representations, which the refined memory layer then transforms into final passage representations.
KAR predicts answer start position and answer end position from refined memories, which are produced after knowledge aided self attention in the refined memory layer.
The AddSent and AddOneSent adversarial sets evaluate the noise robustness problem caused by misleading sentences in evaluation examples.
KAR is evaluated with Exact Match (EM) and F1 score on SQuAD 1.1, whose development examples are used to set INLINEFORM10 through cross validation.

KAR explicitly uses WordNet-derived inter-word semantic connections as general knowledge to assist its attention mechanisms, and replacing those mechanisms lowers F1 on the development set, AddSent, and AddOneSent.

KAR's explicit general-knowledge utilization is claimed to work better than the implicit encoding-based method using Wikipedia and ConceptNet because that best model's development-set EM and F1 are much lower.
The conclusion that KAR is superior in hunger for data is evidenced by KAR performing much better than SAN and QANet on the development set and adversarial sets with training subsets.
The conclusion that KAR is superior in robustness to noise is evidenced by KAR outperforming state-of-the-art MRC models by a large margin on adversarial sets.
KAR's advantage in hunger for data and robustness to noise is jointly supported by training-subset comparisons with SAN and QANet and adversarial-set comparisons with state-of-the-art MRC models.
The WordNet-based data enrichment method supplies the general knowledge whose amount rises monotonically as INLINEFORM0 increases from 0 to 5.
One2Seq concatenates multiple phrases into a delimiter-separated target sequence, enabling self-terminating decoding to determine the proper number of phrases to output.
The fixed-number evaluation setup is problematic because keyphrase generation is a set generation problem with variable set size and variable phrase token size.
The proposed variable-number metrics F INLINEFORM1 @ INLINEFORM2 and F INLINEFORM3 @ INLINEFORM4 remedy the fixed-number evaluation problem by reflecting variable phrase counts per document.

Orthogonal regularization and semantic coverage were proposed to improve diversity, and experiments report that they help the model generate higher quality keyphrases and achieve better generalizability.
One2One models such as CopyRNN generate one phrase at once and must rely on beam search, whereas One2Seq uses a delimiter-concatenated target sequence to generate multiple phrases.
Exhaustive decoding is computationally expensive and wasteful for One2Seq because beam search is costly and less than 5% of phrases generated by One2Seq models are unique.
Self-terminating decoding is applied only to the proposed models because no existing model supports such decoding strategy.
The StackEx benchmark built from StackExchange questions with titles and user-assigned tags challenges models to distill major topics rather than select specific snippets.
On StackEx, INLINEFORM0 performs best and outperforms INLINEFORM1 by a large margin on absent-keyphrase generation tasks.

Because projection based transfer schemes require parallel corpora and Armenian lacked a sufficiently large parallel corpus with a resource-rich language, the authors chose the Wikipedia-link model for automated data generation.
The silver-standard training corpus generated by Sysoev and Andrianov's modification of the Nothman et al. approach was used to train models evaluated on the manually annotated gold dataset.
The strict candidate-sentence selection and relatively small Armenian Wikipedia help explain why the generated corpus has 163247 tokens, significantly smaller than CoNLL 2002 and 2003 corpora.
The conclusion that deep learning approaches achieve relatively high recall is supported by the finding that both deep learning models outperformed the feature-based Stanford recognizer in recall.

The conclusion about character-extracted embeddings alongside conventional word embeddings is supported by the recurrent model's bidirectional LSTM character representation concatenated with GloVe and its highest F1 score.

The CUI-based upper bound analysis tested extractive summarization's assumption that discharge summary information is documented elsewhere and suggested extractive summarization alone may not recreate a discharge summary.
The Learned Word Embeddings model, selected after achieving the highest dev set performance of 0.886, achieved an accuracy of 0.88 and an F1-Score of 0.876 on the test set.
The paper's NN architecture jointly classifies words in history of present illness notes, while the Dernoncourt model jointly classified each sentence in a medical abstract.

The proposed model addresses the less well-understood usefulness of Flickr for characterizing the natural environment by learning location vectors from Flickr tags and structured scientific information.

The paper targets the far-from-optimal concatenation of Flickr tag bag-of-words features and structured scientific data with an embedding model whose components constrain textual, numerical, and categorical information.
Because evaluating the full objective is not computationally feasible with millions of locations and millions of tags, the model samples negative examples rather than considering all tags.
The conclusion that the model integrates Flickr tags with structured information more effectively than existing methods is supported by EGEL-All outperforming the baselines for all considered tasks.

The binary classification tasks of predicting the distribution of 100 species across Europe, soil type, and CORINE land cover classes at levels 1, 2 and level 3 are evaluated using Support Vector Machines (SVMs).

The 26,425 distinct sites occurring in the Natura 2000 dataset define the shared location set INLINEFORM0 used for species distribution, soil type, CORINE land cover, and 5 climate related features experiments.
EGEL-KL(Tags+NS) adds term selection to EGEL-Tags+NS, and term selection leads to particularly substantial improvements for the regression problems.
Pre-ordering English sentences with the CFILT-preorder system to match Indian language word order significantly improves BLEU scores over baseline scores in X-Hindi experiments.
The contextual representation being word-order dependent explains why SVO English and SOV source languages create inconsistent encoder representations that limit transfer learning benefits.

The BLEU score improvements from both pre-ordering configurations provide evidence for the conclusion that pre-ordering the assisting language significantly improves translation quality in an extremely low-resource setting.
The proposed pre-ordering of English sentences to match source-language word order addresses the previously unexplored effect of word order divergence in transfer learning for multilingual NMT.
The finding that pre-ordered models generate fewer UNK tokens supports the BLEU score improvements observed for both pre-ordering configurations.
The current work focused on Indian languages, so the proposed benefit of pre-ordering for other word order divergence scenarios such as SOV to SVO remains unverified.
The unsupervised algorithmic methodology addresses the lack of methodologies for summarising NRLS free text by detecting content-based groups from unstructured incident descriptions.
The framework applies Doc2Vec to the 13 million NRLS records and infers vectors for the 3229 St Mary's Hospital records used for clustering.
Because the NRLS records contain substantial free text and the methodology uses only free and unstructured textual descriptions, the hand-coded structured categories are not required for clustering.
The 15 externally hand-coded categories used in Doc2Vec benchmarking are the top-level categories of the NRLS two-level manual classification system.

The claim that training on smaller sets of 1 million records produces good results is supported by benchmarking where reducing the corpus from 13 million to 1 million records did not affect results dramatically.
MST-kNN sparsification addresses weak, redundant edges that obscure the graph structure in the fully connected weighted graph derived from Doc2Vec similarities.
Markov Stability applied to the MST-kNN graph detects subgraphs corresponding to clusters of documents with similar content at different levels of resolution.
Because MS maximisation is NP-hard, the implementation uses Louvain 500 times at each Markov time and selects the best 50 partitions by r(t,H).
Robust partitions require both high Markov Stability r(t,H) and persistence across time, indicated by VI(t) dips and VI(t,t') extended plateaus.
The $NMI$ score introduced in Eq. ( 8 ) quantifies the correspondence between MS clusters and the hand-coded external categories reflected by two-layer Sankey diagrams.

The $\widehat{PMI}$ score evaluates partitions without requiring a labelled ground truth because it is the weighted average of cluster PMI scores computed from corpus word co-occurrence probabilities.

The $NMI$ used to compare MS partitions against the hand-coded classification is the same score that quantifies correspondence between content clusters and external categories at different resolution levels.
The five MS levels examined in detail with word clouds, Sankey diagrams and contingency tables correspond to robust partitions chosen from finer 44 communities to coarser 3 communities.
The quasi-hierarchical organisation revealed by MS analysis is supported by 12-way communities emerging from consistent aggregation of smaller communities in the 44-way partition.
Word clouds made comprehensible through POS tagging, common-verb removal, lemmatisation and 2 or 3-gram frequency lists were used to derive content labels for the 44-community partition.

Doc2Vec's reported advantages over BoW in semantic similarity benchmarks are confirmed in this framework by the Doc2Vec version outperforming the BoW version across all resolutions in $NMI$ and $\widehat{PMI}$.
Because standard LDA needs a different model trained separately for each pre-determined number of topics, the comparison used five LDA models corresponding to the five MS levels considered in detail.
MS obtains partitions at all resolutions in one sweep of the Markov time, while the five LDA models on the same corpus require 30 hours compared with 13 hours in total for the method.
The method uses paragraph vectors and a content-based similarity graph, and its a posteriori analysis showed good recovery of meaningful categories.

Because local incident reporting systems require risk managers to improve data quality of reports, free text analytical approaches could free risk managers' time from classification and correction by human operators.
The method uses paragraph vectors, while ongoing work requires dynamically managing the embedding of the reports through updates and recalculation of the vector embedding.
The dataset consists of incident reports submitted to the NRLS, and NRLS stands for National Reporting and Learning System.
MTA conducted the computational research and is a PhD student at Imperial College London, Department of Mathematics.
Dedicated Question Answering (QA) systems address the health-information challenge by understanding natural language questions without relying on external information on the users.
Recognizing Question Entailment (RQE) supports Dedicated Question Answering (QA) systems by retrieving entailed questions with associated answers to answer premise questions.
The paper evaluates the end-to-end RQE-based QA approach on TREC 2017 LiveQA medical questions by evaluating the relevance of the retrieved answers.
The inclusion of partial answers in question entailment implements the QA-specific requirement for relevant and meaningful relaxations of contextual and semantic constraints.
The empirical study's Logistic Regression choice is motivated by SemEval 2017 results where the best performing system achieved a MAP of 47.22% using supervised Logistic Regression.
Classifying the full QA collection for each test question is infeasible for real-time applications, so the proposed QA system first uses an IR method to retrieve candidate questions.
The RQE-based QA system requires a collection of question-answer pairs, and the final collection contains 47,457 annotated question-answer pairs extracted from 12 trusted resources.
The question types taxonomy derived from 1,721 consumer health questions supplied the manually defined triggers that were indexed with each question to improve retrieval.
The hybrid IR+RQE QA system achieved 0.827 average score and 0.311 MAP@10 with 0.333 MRR@10, outperforming the IR-based QA system on first-answer and top-10 evaluations.

The evaluation used TREC-2017 LiveQA medical test questions and LiveQA-Med reference answers, and the hybrid IR+RQE QA system achieved a higher score than the best LiveQA'17 medical challenge results.

The RQE-based QA system outperformed the best TREC-2017 LiveQA medical results despite using only 47K medical question-answer pairs while LiveQA participating systems relied on much larger collections, including the World Wide Web.
Because many LiveQA test questions had several subquestions while the system answered one subquestion at most, the hybrid IR+RQE approach has large potential for improvement of answer completeness.
The assessors' report that returned answers had correct question type but wrong focus supports future work on integrating a Question Focus Recognition module to enhance candidate question retrieval.
The need to extend the medical QA collection with more information about drugs is supported by examples where ConsumerLab and eHealthMe answered drug questions when DailyMed lacked information.

Strict guidelines based on information sources or HONcode are supported by experiments showing that limiting the number of answer sources with such guidelines could enhance QA performance from an information retrieval perspective.
The conclusion that the QA approach outperformed the best TREC-2017 LiveQA medical results is evidenced by RQE exceeding the best medical LiveQA'17 challenge results by a factor of 29.8%.

For question number 36 in the TREC-2017 LiveQA medical test dataset, all submitted answers from 5 participating runs were wrong, while the IR-based QA system retrieved one excellent answer and hybrid IR+RQE provided 3 excellent answers.
The proposed model combines $S_1(x,y)$ and $S_2(x,y)$ in Equation 1 with $t$ fixed to $0.25$, and experiments show better results than the baseline using only sentence-keyword similarity.
The baseline is implemented by setting $t$ to 1 in Equation 1, which removes the contribution of $S_2(x,y)$ and leaves only $S_1(x,y)$.
The experimental input is created by randomly rearranging sentences, matching the paper's task of segmenting an unordered text document into different sections.

Directly fine-tuning neural networks pretrained as language models predicts all six ERP components above chance, whereas prior linking-function work successfully linked language models only to the N400 and P600.
Because BIBREF7 related language models to EEG through a priori functions, the paper speculates that its direct LSTM prediction of the P600 reveals information those interpretable functions lost.
The six ERP components analyzed from BIBREF0 include N400, EPNP, and PNP as semantic markers and P600, ELAN, and LAN as syntactic markers, and all six can be predicted above chance.
PHASE-TWO leave-one-subject out cross-validation on KARA ONE still achieved improvements of 18.91, 9.95, 67.15, 2.83 and 13.70 % over BIBREF17.
The DAE trained on fused CNN and LSTM features improves classification accuracy by a mean margin of 14.45% over the CNN-LSTM network.
Channel cross-covariance matrices encoding electrode connectivity are the input from which CNN decodes spatial connections and LSTM explores hidden temporal features.

The joint spatio-temporal encoding of the cross-covariance matrix is further reduced by the DAE before its discrete latent vector representation is fed into the Extreme Gradient Boost based classification layer.
NeuronBlocks addresses engineers' productivity and less optimal solution challenges with a two-layer design that balances generality and flexibility.
The upper layer and bottom layer in the Introduction correspond to the Model Zoo and Block Zoo in the Design section.
NeuronBlocks' two-layer design responds to prior toolkits being limited to certain tasks and not flexible enough for new architectures or components.
The Model Architecture interface implements the workflow's Block Zoo construction path by defining a list of layers/blocks from the Block Zoo gallery.
The knowledge distillation template's goal of improving inference speed is supported by the student model's 23-27 times inference speedup on Domain Classification Dataset.
NeuronBlocks' claim of reliable and competitive results on various tasks is evidenced by competitive or even better results on GLUE tasks and WikiQA dataset.

The strategy of routing difficult instances to domain experts and easier ones to crowd annotators is evaluated by expert re-annotation of 1000 top-ranked difficult abstracts and 1000 randomly sampled abstracts.
The conclusion that crowd annotation supplements expert annotations for medical IE is evidenced by mixed annotations improving at least 1 point F1 score in all three extraction tasks.
The greater gain from routing according to difficulty is supported by D+Other outperforming R+Other by 2 points in F1 and by the 3.5 F1 score improvement.
The attention models proposed to infer latent context are evaluated on a corpus of 12 MOOC discussion forums.
Because the actual instructor intervention is unavailable at decision timing, UPA uses the most recent content in the thread as the attentional query for context.
APA's relaxation to any previous post as a query is consistent with its better prediction on longer threads, which possess more candidate contexts.
The debiasing approach does not explicitly address the bias in the embedding layer, yet end-to-end debiasing of the language model can achieve word embedding debiasing.

The adaptive multi-task learning setup is supported by empirical results showing modified Kneser-Ney smoothing performs best on single-token hashtags while Good-Turing and Linguistic features work best on multi-token hashtags.
The MSE+multitask model's 24.6% error reduction over the previous SOTA on Multi-token hashtags is evaluated with segmentation-level accuracy requiring full matches to human segmentation.
Because the approach heavily relies on a Twitter language model trained on 1.1 billion tweets, reducing it to 10% and 1% causes F INLINEFORM0 score drops of only 1.4% and 3.9%.
Although language use in Twitter changes with time, the pairwise ranker trained on tweets from 2010 performs favorably on 500 random English hashtags from 2019 with 94.6% segmentation-level accuracy.
HashtagMaster segmentation was evaluated with BiLSTM+Lex on the SemEval 2017 subtask A test set, where 3,384 tweets had split hashtags.
The conclusion that hashtag segmentation helps sentiment analysis is supported by HashtagMaster improving BiLSTM+Lex average recall and F INLINEFORM0 by 2% on 3,384 tweets.
HashtagMaster's segmentation is especially important for the 125 tweets whose sentiment words occur only in hashtags, since BiLSTM+Lex predicts tweet-level sentiment from tweet text.

The paper's broader claim that automatic hashtag segmentation can improve applications besides sentiment analysis is complemented by its demonstrated sentiment analysis improvement with HashtagMaster.
The McGurk-style illusion method of pairing unmodified audio with mismatched visual dubs produced an average miscomprehension rate of 24.8% in word-level experiments.
The McGurk-style illusion method of pairing unmodified audio with mismatched visual dubs produced an average miscomprehension rate of 32.8% in sentence-level experiments.
The claim that illusionability of words and sentences can be predicted using features from natural language modeling is supported by out-of-sample correlations of 57% and 33%.
The word-level model using illusionable phonemes enriched with positional information achieved an out-of-sample correlation of 57% between predicted and observed illusionabilites.
The proposed reduced vocabulary defense for neural networks susceptible to the McGurk effect requires the word-level illusionability prediction model.
The conclusion that human perception can be altered for a significant fraction of natural speech is supported by word-level and sentence-level miscomprehension rates of 24.8% and 32.8%.
PARENT addresses divergent references by using a union of the reference and the table for precision and an intersection for recall.
The WikiBio human evaluation found references scored lower than PG-Net, supporting the claim that WikiBio contains many divergent references.
PARENT-W is the word-overlap model and is significantly better than the other two highest-correlation metrics for systems.
On WebNLG, PARENT does best for semantics, which corresponds to agreement with the meaning of the underlying RDF triples.
The 8800 pairwise comparisons from 1100 tables were aggregated by Thurstone's method into real-valued scores for correlation with automatic metrics.
The information extraction PG-Net trained for WikiBio with a beam size of 8 and no length penalty can be used for evaluating generated texts despite hallucinating some false information.
The divergent references that motivate PARENT also limit the WikiBio information extraction model, which cannot be expected to produce the entire table and hallucinates some false information.

The inverse information extraction PG-Net shares the same tuned hyperparameters as the table-to-text PG-Net, including 50000-word vocabularies, Glove BIBREF43 embeddings, 40-token decoded text, and 120-token tables.
The manually compiled 600 trilingual sentences test set was used for evaluating MT models with case-sensitive and tokenized BLEU BIBREF23.
The M2M Transformer NMT model (b3), examined to cope with the low-resource problem, outperformed standard PBSMT models (c1) and all pivot-based approaches with uni-directional NMT models.
The final multistage fine-tuning models V and VII achieved significantly higher BLEU scores than the M2M Transformer NMT model (b3), which had outperformed standard PBSMT models (c1).
The BLEU scores for Ja INLINEFORM2 Ru and Ru INLINEFORM3 Ja not exceeding 10 BLEU points motivated exploring other types of parallel data.
Because no out-of-domain data is available for Ja INLINEFORM1 Ru, the proposed multistage fine-tuning method exploits out-of-domain Ja INLINEFORM2 En and Ru INLINEFORM3 En pairs.
The M2M Transformer NMT model (b3) selected for back-translation generated six-way pseudo-parallel data whose all-direction use (#10) improved the base model except En INLINEFORM0 Ru.
The further back-translation experiment used identical monolingual sentences sampled in Section SECREF34 and repeated generation and fine-tuning five times.
The fine-tuned model VIII surpassed the base NMT model VII, while “new #10” trained from scratch on six-way pseudo-parallel data underperformed VII.
Because no good quality dataset existed to train NER, the authors created OurNepali dataset from daily newspaper sentences of 2015-2016 and released it to support future research.
The neural based Nepali NER proposed to avoid hand-crafted features was evaluated on the dataset that we created and on the dataset received from ILPRL lab.
FastText embeddings were chosen for their sub-word representation ability, and the model using fastText_Skip Gram embeddings outperforms all other models on OurNepali dataset.
Lemmatizing post-positions boosted the F1 score by almost 10%, supporting the discussion that stemming post-positions can help a lot in improving model performance.
The dropout of 0.5 applied after LSTM layer was chosen because the F1 score starts falling down after dropout rate = 0.5.
Because OurNepali dataset volume is almost ten times bigger compared to ILPRL dataset in terms of entities, the authors conclude that more data is needed to get better results.
Because MP iterations correspond to network depth and basic MPAD uses two MP iterations ($T$=2), basic MPAD has depth two.
With two MP iterations ($T$=2), basic MPAD final vertex representations are based on messages propagated from subtrees of height 2 rooted at each vertex.
The multi-readout applied to all time steps takes into account local and global features because node features capture more and more global information as one iterates.
The hierarchical MPAD variants are compared fairly against hierarchical baselines including LSTM-GRNN BIBREF26 and HN-ATT.
The experimental directed word co-occurrence network built from each document with a window of size 2 implements MPAD's statistical word co-occurrence network with a sliding window of size 2.

MPAD reaches best performance on 7 out of 10 datasets, supporting the conclusion that experiments on 10 standard text classification datasets show the architecture is competitive with the state-of-the-art.
One or more hierarchical variants outperform vanilla MPAD on 9 datasets out of 10, supporting the conclusion that three hierarchical variants bring improvements over the vanilla architecture.
